note: Teraflex 2.5-inch kit with cam bolts and an adjustable track bar; buy a JT-specific kit, and skip spacers if 35s are the plan.
Rock Hard 4x4 bolt-on at $449; a JL slider will not cover the JT's longer rocker.
Teraflex JT kit covers engine, transmission and transfer case. A Rubicon already has front axle and transfer case plates.
Five 35x12.50R17 all-terrains at about $420 each; they clear at 2.5 inches of lift, though full lock may still touch.
Rough Country at about $499; check for front parking sensors and a forward camera, which budget bumpers often skip.
Warn VR EVO 10-S; 10,000 pounds is the minimum for a JT's 5,400 to 6,200 pound GVWR.
Bilstein stabilizer for 35s; it damps shimmy but does not fix worn steering parts.
Heavy-duty tie rod and drag link for 35s and up; fix worn steering parts before blaming the stabilizer.
A receiver D-ring mount at about $20; the steel front bumper already carries rated tabs.
Both Dana 44s together, 4.56 for 35s, at the 35-inch guide's $1,200 to $2,000 shop price. A Rubicon's 4.10s can wait.
Eaton ELocker needs no compressor. Skip on a Rubicon, Mojave or 2024 Willys, which have a factory rear locker.
Rough Country with a 2-inch hitch; the JT spare lives under the bed, so there is no carrier to buy.
Rock Krawler 3.5-inch mid-arm, the lift 37s need; it must be a JT-specific kit, not a JL kit.
Redo at 4.88 for 37s, which the 37s guide calls mandatory; this replaces the 4.56 set.
Five 37s at about $280 each; expect fender trimming, and budget about $235 for a tire-size programmer.
